data.title: Nepal: 'Region has hundreds of high-altitude lakes prone to unleashing enormous volumes of water'
data.description: William Hilderbrandt is pleased to welcome David Fisher, Head of Delegation, Nepal International Federation of Red Cross. The scale of Nepal’s disaster cannot yet be fully measured. Entire communities remain difficult to reach, tens of thousands of people have been affected, and official assessments are only beginning. But the central challenge is already clear: this cannot be treated solely as an immediate humanitarian emergency. What happens to these communities in the years ahead depends heavily on what we do now. Emergency relief must be accompanied from the outset by planning, funding and action for long-term recovery, including rebuilding homes and livelihoods. If that work is postponed until international attention has moved elsewhere, many people may never fully recover. And signs suggest that the speed and destructive force of this extreme natural event could become more frequent.

data.title: ‘I don’t want to be a backseat driver’: Gordon Brown on Burnham, billionaires – and his vision for a better Britain
data.description: The former UK prime minister is still shaping politics (even if he doesn’t want to interfere). He talks about keeping his temper, staying fit – and why he won’t pay £90 for a Scotland football shirt It’s a Monday in August and as England burns in dystopian heat, Gordon Brown and I are in his office at the top of his house in North Queensferry, overlooking the moody waters of the Firth of Forth. It’s hard to recall the top of my own sauna-like house in London as we stand here in the cool, wearing wool suits and necessary socks, my coat slung over the back of a chair. “I was watching Raith Rovers – the local football team – on Saturday,” Brown says, “and it was really cold. There was a wind blowing in from the sea.” He asks if I’ve heard the famous joke – “Scotland’s only got two seasons: July and winter”– then chuckles. It’s one of his favourites. (I’ll hear him tell it three times today.) That’s not to say Fife has been untouched by the multiple heatwaves. They had a few sunny days. One hit 24C – “a shock”, Brown says, July temperatures typically being 15-17C. He stood in his kitchen and considered the modest patch of grass at the back of the house. “I never imagined being out in the garden in the summer. I never imagined it because it’s either raining or too cold.” Once out, he found himself battling a “very dangerous” nest of wasps. One family member was stung, then there was the rigmarole of specialists in thick gloves and protective suits undertaking its removal. By the time that was done, the sun had gone in. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘The flood took everything I have’: survivors grieve for relatives and homes swept away in Nepal
data.description: Army helicopters ferry survivors from inaccessible areas to a camp at a barracks in Bidur The three women sat together in the army tent and wept. They cried out for their sons, their husbands, their homes. As flash floods coursed through the Himalayan mountains on Wednesday morning, a monstrous black wave took everything from them. As a melting glacier high up in the Himalayas between Tibet and Nepal splintered and crashed into the valley below, it set off a deadly cascade of water, mud and debris down the Bhote Koshi River. The impact of the glacier collapse was so strong that experts initially reported it as an earthquake. The Nepali village homes that lined the riverbank and clung to the mountainside stood little chance. Continue reading...

data.title: The battle over RAF Barnham: how ominous anti-asylum protests engulfed a small Norfolk town
data.description: Thetford has a welcoming history. So why have there been so many demonstrations this summer over plans to house asylum seekers at a nearby military base – as well as nights of violent disorder? ‘I don’t talk to mainstream media,” says a young man in an Arsenal shirt. I’ve just asked what brought him to the latest protest against the housing of asylum seekers in Thetford, Norfolk, and his disdain is clear as he goes to warn other protesters of the Guardian’s presence. This isn’t exactly the unity promised by the flyer advertising today’s march: “Everyone welcome: families, friends, dogs. Including the media.” The protest is planned as a two-mile march from Thetford’s market square to RAF Barnham, a site just over the border in Suffolk, which is due to house asylum seekers while they progress through the system. It is the latest part of a campaign that has lasted the whole summer. Banners line the square, the largest succinctly describing why people are gathering here today: “Thetford and Barnham says no to asylum seekers.” Continue reading...

data.title: Charli xcx, Reading Festival review – Pretentious? Just a bit. But Nietzsche would have loved it
data.description: Reading Festival There’s not much time to dig into her deep catalogue of future-facing pop, but she satisfies the hardcore “Time itself is a circle,” as the rock’n’roll philosopher Nietzsche once said, accurately foreshadowing Charli xcx’s only UK festival appearance this summer. Like her performance on Glastonbury’s Other Stage last year – a pyrotechnic farewell to the puke-green reign of Brat – Charli’s Reading and Leeds appearance is a not-quite-headline slot that also follows a rowdy set from grime don Skepta. Yet in the past 14 months, everything else in Charli’s pop factory has undergone a hard reset. She’s released two albums – a grandiose, gothic soundtrack to Emerald Fennell’s adaptation of Wuthering Heights, and last month’s high-concept Music, Fashion, Film, an album of raw, glitching micro-rock, with guitars shredded into Tetris-like pieces, and fitted with lacerating lyrics about shopping, egotism and mortality. She’s also launched an acting career, thrown a big fat celebrity wedding and, somewhere along the way, found time to rehearse her biggest, most vertiginous show to date. Continue reading...

data.title: Sunsets, disasters, dinners: we now record them all with our phones. But what is that doing to our souls? | Phoebe Greenwood
data.description: As a war correspondent, I worked with photographers who said the camera was a buffer between them and reality. It is much the same now as we snap and scroll I was sitting on a rooftop in Athens at sunset looking up at Filopappou hill. Athens in August is burning hot . Not so much hotter than London or Paris any more, but the sort of hot that makes it foolish to step out into sunlight before 6pm. Emerging from the air conditioning at dusk, I saw a dense line of silhouettes on the ridge above me. Almost every one of these shadows had its arm raised, holding a cameraphone towards the sunset. Of all the pretty hills in the Greek capital, Filopappou arguably has the best view. The Acropolis stands directly to its north. To its south, where I sat, the city sprawls out towards the sea and a dark horizon of islands – Aegina, Salamina, Agistri. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘The butcher may be gone, but to many he is a hero’: victims condemn glorification of Mladić
data.description: Architect of Srebrenica genocide is dead but those scarred by his atrocities say his ideology is still shockingly pervasive To most of the world, he was and will always be the “Butcher of Bosnia”, a grim epithet but one that still fails to fully convey the evil and horror inflicted on its people by Gen Ratko Mladić, who died in prison on Thursday . As commander of the Bosnian Serb forces, Mladić was responsible for the killing of an estimated 100,000 men, women and children during the savage breakup of Yugoslavia in the 1990s. He was most notoriously the architect of ethnic cleansing and the genocide at Srebrenica in which at least 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys were slaughtered. Continue reading...

data.description: ‘At a time when Russia is trying to spread gloom and darkness … it is important to create something beautiful,’ says combat medic Tetiana as she weds army captain Oleksandr In the bright early afternoon sun of Kramatorsk’s central and now ironically named Peace Square, Tetiana, in her bridal dress, and Oleksandr, in his military uniform, are holding up their phones at the ready. It is a public holiday, 35 years since Ukraine’s declaration of independence, and a popular day for a wedding, though the open-air location is not obviously ideal. Three days earlier, Kramatorsk, perhaps Vladimir Putin’s principal target, was formally designated part of the combat zone, the front inching towards the city as Russia closes in on the parts of the Donetsk region it does not control. It is quiet at 2pm though; the ceremony brief. There are no guests other than the Guardian team. Tetiana and Oleksandr pose for a wedding photo on Mount Karachun, near Sloviansk, the scene of fierce fighting in 2014. Continue reading...

data.title: How to make a bestseller: insiders reveal the tricks of the book trade
data.description: From cover design to shelf placement and influencer partnerships … how publishers will persuade you to buy their books this autumn Think about the last book you bought. How did you choose it? Was it from a recommendation, a review, a TikTok video? Did the cover grab you, were you swayed by the quotes on the front, or did you just happen to spot it on an appealing table as you walked into the shop? Did you think about all the nudges that led you to that decision – by the publisher, the bookseller or that person you follow on Insta? The reality is that our reading choices are directed and massaged at every turn. “It’s all about the art of persuasion,” says Philip Gwyn Jones, who was a publisher for more than 30 years and is now a literary agent. And who are the persuaders? They’re the booksellers, the supermarket stock buyers, the publishing houses and their ranks of marketers and publicists. And, more recently, persuasion often comes from BookTokers and online influencers, social media videos, podcasts and Instagram posts. How is all this changing publishing? Continue reading...

data.title: Flipping marvellous: Yotam Ottolenghi on the joy of simple breakfasts – plus six exclusive recipes
data.description: Weekend mornings are for family – and whoever happens to be over. Forget fussing and focus on just one big lovely thing for the middle of the table. Here’s how Family life has had a bigger impact on how I cook at home than almost anything else. There’s a lot of pasta on the menu these days, and potato wedges with different sauces. A lot of meatballs. And a great many pancakes – more than I would have ever predicted before I had kids. My weekend pancakes – which made their way into my book Simple Too – are supposed to be a batch-cooking exercise: lots made on Sunday, then reheated through the week, in the toaster or a dry pan on the stove, so breakfast is more or less solved until Friday. That’s the theory. In practice, all 22 pancakes the recipe makes are gone by Sunday lunch – eaten by the boys, their friends, or whoever happens to be over for breakfast. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘In walked this big bundle of energy’: the day Dolly Parton came to Rotherham
data.description: Country star came to South Yorkshire town in 2007 for UK launch of the Imagination Library, her book donation scheme Shane Jarman was up a ladder decorating a Christmas tree at the school where he was deputy headteacher when he got a call asking him to come to Rotherham hospital ASAP. It was December 2007 and Jarman’s wife, Claire, had given birth the previous day to their first child, a girl called Emma, so of course he rushed to the phone. All was well, he was told, but that “everything would become clear” when he got to the hospital. Once there, his wife told him – somewhat unexpectedly – that they were going to meet Dolly Parton. “And literally within what felt like five minutes,” he recalled, “there were great camera flashes , lots of noise, lots of clicking and in walked this real big bundle of energy.” Continue reading...

data.title: A slow travel success story in Slovenia’s secret valley
data.description: Tourism is only just taking hold in Vipava, but the locals are determined to do it right, by putting community first and preserving what makes it special The drive to Pedrovo is vertiginous, and each hairpin bend has me sending a silent prayer that we won’t meet a tractor coming the other way. When we near it, we abandon the car and continue on foot to the hamlet, a scattering of red-roofed, whitewashed houses high on the steep karst hillside. The air is warm and dry, scented with wild sage. We follow a hand-painted sign to Čilčevi Farmstead. Descending stone steps to a lush garden, we find a shaded table set with fresh cheeses produced at the farm’s own dairy. Below, the valley stretches in both directions, a wide flat plain hemmed in by steep mountain slopes, with the Vipava River winding lazily through fields and vineyards. Continue reading...

data.title: The hill I will die on: The barbecue is fundamentally unenjoyable. Please, put a lid on it | Max Liu
data.description: Dress up the barbie however you like – it’s toxic, tiresome and, more to the point, malnourishing “If you’re invited to a barbecue, have your dinner before you go.” It is the wisest advice my dad has ever given me. Barbecues are one of life’s perennial disappointments. The romance of eating outside quickly degenerates into a recipe for mucky fingers, smelly clothes and more mess than you bargained for , with grills that you can never get clean, uncomfortable seating that makes your back ache or, dafter still, eating while standing up. Worst of all is the true barbecue legacy – the nagging hunger that follows bitty dining, leaving you with the aggrieved sense that you missed a mealtime you’re never getting back. I grew up in Cornwall, where beach barbecues were a rite of passage. The flame under the sandy grill was blown out by the Atlantic wind, so these gatherings were impractical, unpredictable and interminable. One minute the sausages were raw and looked like they’d never be ready, the next they were hard and black and basically inedible. Rain frequently sent us scrambling to pack up and flee for shelter. Max Liu is a freelance writer Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on the loan of the Bayeux tapestry: a manifestation of soft power | Editorial
data.description: The British Museum’s landmark cultural exchange is a symbol of post-Brexit rapprochement between Britain and France “ Harold Rex interfectus est ”: King Harold is killed. As every British schoolchild knows, the Bayeux tapestry depicts a turning point in the history of these islands: defeat at the Battle of Hastings in 1066, which would lead to the ascent of William the Conqueror to the English throne. Its return to the UK for the first time in nearly 1,000 years is being hailed as a hugely historic moment in its own right. The loan of the tapestry (technically an embroidery of wool on linen) to the British Museum in exchange for UK treasures from Sutton Hoo is the ultimate manifestation of soft power – a 70-metre symbol of post-Brexit Anglo-French rapprochement in comic-strip form. Ticket sales for the exhibition, which opens on 10 September, were the biggest in a single day in the museum’s history , with online queues of 80,000. Radio 4 is devoting a day of special broadcasts to mark the arrival of the tapestry, including a new drama with verse from the poet laureate Simon Armitage. The museum’s videos explaining this tale of ambition, friendship, betrayal and revenge are fittingly narrated by Traitors presenter Claudia Winkleman. Norman-mania is here. data.title: The Guardian view on political donations: Labour should curb the power of big money | Editorial
data.description: Before becoming prime minister, Andy Burnham favoured a £500,000 donations cap. In office, he’s backing away. That is a mistake On the campaign trail in Makerfield, Andy Burnham told a democracy activist that he favoured a political donations cap of around £500,000 and wanted it reduced over time. His government is now resisting amendments that would move in precisely that direction. Mr Burnham was right in May . He is wrong now. It is difficult to argue that restricting a single person to giving half a million pounds a year to a political party would damage democracy. Such a cap would only affect the mega-rich . Reducing the cap would force parties to wean themselves off the present regime that allows the rich too much say. There are two contra arguments swilling around Labour. The first is that there should be room for wealthy, progressive donors – whose cash helps rebut claims that Labour is in the pocket of the trade unions. The second is the warning from unions that a cap could undermine their ability to contribute to the Labour party. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: ‘Now is a good time for players to speak up’: Lucy Bronze on Fifa and helping refugees
data.description: Chelsea defender reflects on spending time with refugees in Colombia this summer and her passion for helping people on and off the pitch Lucy Bronze does not stop. Her brain runs a hundred miles a minute. She does not need traditional entertainment. “I’m not good at watching TV – I can’t sit still,” Bronze says, sitting sort-of still, on a bench shielded from the wind, overlooking Chelsea’s training pitch at Cobham. “Someone recently asked me what I listen to in the car and someone else jumped in and was like: ‘Lucy has her own podcast going on in her own head.’ I don’t listen to music, I don’t listen to podcasts, I just have a million thoughts going on.” Bronze’s late ADHD and autism diagnosis help it make sense, but her mum had always suspected she might have one of the conditions, so it wasn’t a surprise. “Naomi Girma said to me: ‘I’ve never met someone who trains so hard in the gym with zero music on; it does not make sense.’ I was like: ‘It’s literally in my head, I don’t need anything else.’” Continue reading...

She does not need traditional entertainment. “I’m not good at watching TV – I can’t sit still,” Bronze says, sitting sort-of still, on a bench shielded from the wind, overlooking Chelsea’s training pitch at Cobham. “Someone recently asked me what I listen to in the car and someone else jumped in and was like: ‘Lucy has her own podcast going on in her own head.’ I don’t listen to music, I don’t listen to podcasts, I just have a million thoughts going on.” Bronze’s late ADHD and autism diagnosis help it make sense, but her mum had always suspected she might have one of the conditions, so it wasn’t a surprise. “Naomi Girma said to me: ‘I’ve never met someone who trains so hard in the gym with zero music on; it does not make sense.’ I was like: ‘It’s literally in my head, I don’t need anything else.’” Continue reading...

data.title: Carlos Alcaraz believes ‘it is possible’ to win US Open despite long injury layoff
data.description: The 23-year-old has not competed in singles since April Defending champion faces Roman Safiullin in first round Carlos Alcaraz believes he is capable of winning the US Open as he returns to professional tennis after a four-month injury layoff due to a right wrist injury. Alcaraz, the defending champion in New York, will compete in singles for the first time since injuring his wrist at the Barcelona Open in April when he faces Roman Safiullin in the first round. “So, it is possible [to win],” Alcaraz said. “I think that many people have shown it. [Roger] Federer, [Rafa] Nadal, many people have shown that you can win a grand slam after having been injured for a long time or having had a very hard injury. So we’re going to try to tie ourselves to that belief that we can do it too.” Continue reading...

data.title: Esther González, Saudi Arabia and the questions around an unexpected transfer saga
data.description: The Gotham striker said she was stepping away from the sport, but then signed for Al Qadsiah. The move sparked questions over professionalism and raised concerns of LGBTQ+ fans who have disavowed the Saudi league A recent World Cup winner joins a historically downtrodden club, immediately leads them to their first championship, praises the level of play in the league, speaks fondly of living in the club’s market, extends her contract with the club, leads the club to another championship, is named a league MVP finalist, and breaks the club’s all-time scoring record. That’s the fairytale of Esther González and Gotham FC – a story that ended abruptly, just nine days after that scoring record was set. On 27 July, Gotham announced that they had mutually parted ways with the striker as she “temporarily steps away from soccer to attend to personal matters in Spain”. The announcement of her departure was full of gushing words going both directions, and was met with understanding and support from the women’s soccer world. But less than a month after González left Gotham, Al Qadsiah, a club in the Saudi Women’s Premier League, announced her as their newest signing, on a one-season contract with an option to extend for a second. NWSL journalist Jenna Tonelli soon reported , “League sources tell me that Gotham did not expect Esther to sign with another club this soon.” Questions swirled: did she actually intend to take a break from soccer when she left Gotham? And why would a player who just had a child with her female partner choose to play in Saudi Arabia, a country where same-sex relations are criminalized? Continue reading...

data.title: Statins can safely cut risk of heart attacks or strokes in healthy people aged over 70, world-first clinical trial shows
data.description: Australian-led trial finds low risk of side effects from common cholesterol-lowering medication for otherwise healthy older people Taking a common cholesterol-lowering medication can reduce the risk of a heart attack or stroke for people aged over 70, with a low risk of serious side effects, a world-first clinical trial led by Australian researchers has found. Statins are already commonly prescribed to people under the age of 75 who meet certain risk criteria, such as having diabetes and high cholesterol, to prevent them from having a major heart event such as a heart attack, stroke, or from requiring heart surgery. data.title: They laid down arms. Now ex-guerrillas in Colombia fear fate under new hardline president
data.description: ‘Total peace’ plan of previous government led only 99 of Colombia’s 30,000 armed combatants to disarm, but new president Abelardo De la Espriella opposes peace agreements In mid-June, 99 guerrilla fighters were flown by helicopter to a small settlement in a rural area of southern Colombia where they lined up and, one by one, handed their weapons to government officials: rifles, pistols, machine guns and grenade launchers. They also stripped off their heavy tactical vests, field packs and camouflage uniforms, which were each piled into a bonfire to mark the beginning of a new life away from an armed conflict that has claimed nearly half a million lives in the last six decades. data.title: In South Korea, it is illegal to travel to dangerous countries. Journalists say it’s making their work impossible
data.description: Penalties for travel to blacklisted countries have recently risen, while aid workers and activists say they have also been caught up in the law Shortly after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, freelance photographer Jang Jinyoung crossed from Poland into Lviv and travelled on to Kyiv, where he spent a fortnight documenting the war. South Korea’s foreign ministry had designated Ukraine off-limits days earlier, making unauthorised visits a criminal offence. He knew he was breaking the law but went anyway, as no Korean journalist had yet reported from inside the country. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian climate pledge 2026
data.description: Each year, the Guardian reaffirms its commitment to the environment – both in our reporting and how we operate as a business. From critical tipping points to war in Iran, this is how the last 12 months have looked Support the Guardian’s environment coverage The Guardian climate forum 2026 Today marks the end of the Guardian’s annual climate support campaign. Each year, during the campaign, we remind our audience about the Guardian’s role in covering the threats to our planet and the importance of independent journalism in telling that story. Our climate pledge is a reminder of the environmental values we place at the heart of our reporting and our organisation. Since our 2025 climate pledge , the world has experienced extreme levels of heat as well as extreme forms of denial and abdication in the face of the climate crisis. But, across the world, there have also been inspiring efforts to tackle it. We will be publishing our annual company emissions data in the autumn, explaining what drives our emissions and where they have risen and fallen. We have started the process of estimating our emissions from generative AI usage. We hope to report on this next year. We have undertaken our B Corp recertification in line with the new standards introduced by B Lab in 2026. We will find out our result later this year. We have participated in advertising industry working groups that published a methodological framework that aims to capture the emissions impact of digital and print advertising. We open ourselves up to scrutiny by independent third parties, such as the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) and B Corp, so they can assess the robustness of our targets and our internal policies. Continue reading...

data.title: The chefs turning down the heat by switching from gas to electric
data.description: As well as being quieter, cheaper to run and easier to clean, induction cookers can cut kitchen temperatures by up to 10C Leaping flames, searing heat, copious sweat and scorchingly inventive swearing – restaurant kitchens are never a place for the faint-hearted, but this summer they have been sweltering in successive heatwaves to a dangerous degree. Some restaurants, cafes and bakeries in the UK grew so hot that they were forced to close , or reduce their hours , for the safety of their staff. There is still no maximum working temperature, despite calls from the TUC , and tens of thousands of kitchen staff are thought to have carried on working in “furnace-like” conditions . data.title: Chris Cantrill: Rewilding review – a rural whodunnit told with midlife mirth
data.description: Monkey Barrel Comedy, Edinburgh Cantrill shares his struggles descending into middle age and his awkward interactions with fellow villagers in a fun show Now a four-time nominee for the Edinburgh comedy award , Chris Cantrill is bearing down on James Acaster’s always-the-bridesmaid record – unless 2026 proves to be his year. Would it be merited? Well, there are few comedians in whose company it is more reliably fun to spend time. And that’s resoundingly the case with Rewilding, the follow-up to 2024’s Easily Swayed , in which Cantrill gave an uproarious account of turning 40, moving to the countryside and having (the male, northern, emotionally stunted equivalent of) a breakdown. The sequel is scarcely less entertaining, but it’s not as well constructed, and its story is less resonant. It begins with this ebullient Bradford native explaining how bad he is at introducing himself, with reference to “drinks and nibs” his wife has coerced him to attend in their Northumbrian village. Cantrill is chronic at small talk, he tells us, yet adept at code-switching – as demonstrated in the company of the “gen Z girls and gays” who love him, rural workers whose opinions he meekly opposes in the pub, and the private-school boys who (as per one gloriously indiscreet section) call the shots where Cantrill works, on Saturday Night Live UK . At Monkey Barrel Comedy, Edinburgh , until 30 August All our Edinburgh festival reviews Continue reading...

And that’s resoundingly the case with Rewilding, the follow-up to 2024’s Easily Swayed , in which Cantrill gave an uproarious account of turning 40, moving to the countryside and having (the male, northern, emotionally stunted equivalent of) a breakdown. The sequel is scarcely less entertaining, but it’s not as well constructed, and its story is less resonant. It begins with this ebullient Bradford native explaining how bad he is at introducing himself, with reference to “drinks and nibs” his wife has coerced him to attend in their Northumbrian village. Cantrill is chronic at small talk, he tells us, yet adept at code-switching – as demonstrated in the company of the “gen Z girls and gays” who love him, rural workers whose opinions he meekly opposes in the pub, and the private-school boys who (as per one gloriously indiscreet section) call the shots where Cantrill works, on Saturday Night Live UK . At Monkey Barrel Comedy, Edinburgh , until 30 August All our Edinburgh festival reviews Continue reading...

data.title: The Rainmaker review – please don’t hurt your eyes trying to find anything good in this legal drama
data.description: From dialogue so hokey it could be printed on a tea towel to mind-numbing storylines – how can a glossy take on John Grisham’s novel about a fiery law graduate be so tedious? The Rainmaker was once merely an average film about lawyers starring Matt Damon. Now, thanks to the magic of television, it’s a below-average series about lawyers starring a man who looks like Matt Damon. This is one Milo Callaghan, whose jawline suggests a certain mettle, but whose acting suggests much woe. Or at least a fitful unease with the role in which he finds himself. Accordingly, he drifts around this 10-part John Grisham adaptation with the air of a man who has forgotten what he came into the courtroom for, certain only that whatever it was, it was not a drama that compels him to say things like: “Ah just wanna be a lawyer.” Callaghan plays Rudy Baylor, an ambitious South Carolina law graduate with a social conscience and a thirst for justice. Rudy wants to make a difference but dammit if his fiery temper don’t keep conspirin’ to screw up his plans. The huffing greenhorn is even late for his first day at prestigious law firm Tinley Britt, having spent the morning hurling his mom’s lunkish boyfriend around the garden (“You think ah’m gonna let you keep leechin’ off ma mother? Gnyaaarrr! ”). Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I don’t care if I look good’: French heartthrob Louis Garrel on fashion, fatherhood and his radically dorky new role
data.description: The star has long been French cinema’s favourite tousle-haired Adonis, which makes his latest performance – as a schlubby, stay-at-home dad – all the more surprising. ‘I appreciate people laughing at me,’ he says ‘Even though I’ve been working in film for over 20 years, I still have this desire to look beautiful on screen,” says Louis Garrel, on a video call from his bed inside a boat off the coast of Corsica. The French film star is lying on his stomach, occasionally kicking up his bare legs, ruffling his curls and running the nail of his thumb over his moustache. I think the person he sees on the laptop screen in front of him is me, but I am pretty certain he is flirting with his own reflection. The attraction between the Paris-born 43-year-old and the camera tends to be reciprocal. Long of limb, tousled of hair and chiselled of nose, Garrel has spent a career on screen as French cinema’s favourite Adonis – the man film-makers turn to when they need an erotic wrecking ball to smash up bourgeois twosomes and turn them into quivering menages a trois. Continue reading...

data.title: Add to playlist: the spectral, fathoms-deep folksong of June McDoom and the week’s best new tracks
data.description: Rich harmonies mix with synth, harp and aquatic grace on the intriguing first single from the New York songwriter’s debut album From New York, USA Recommended if you like Jessica Pratt, Minnie Riperton, Cocteau Twins Up next Debut LP Follow the Light released via Jagjaguwar on 16 October In Robert Silverberg’s 1973 sci-fi anthology New Dimensions 3, there’s a story by author Terry Carr called They Live on Levels. The simplest outline of this tale is that thanks to a technological breakthrough, humans are able to exist and communicate through different planes of existence. Through musical styles and generational layers, the spectral folk of New York-based songwriter June McDoom expresses this very notion in stunning fashion. Continue reading...

data.title: The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past – Geralt of Rivia returns after a decade in the sun
data.description: Before The Witcher 4 arrives in 2028, CD Projekt Red is returning us to the world of The Witcher 3 for one last foray. Looks like wind’s still howlin’ The game that graced us with Bathtub Geralt , The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, arrived more than a decade ago. So it was a touch surprising this summer when developers CD Projekt Red announced a new expansion to the venerable adventure, titled Songs of the Past, for next year. It will release alongside a full remaster of the original game, which will be free for anyone who bought it back in 2015. (The studio is also working on a sequel, The Witcher 4, but that’s not due until 2028.) As it turns out, this is all possible thanks to a partnership with Fool’s Theory, a studio founded by CD Projekt Red veterans, which took on the brunt of the development work. “We’ve had this story in a drawer for many years,” explains Marcin Blacha, VP story director at CD Projekt Red. “Of course, we moved on to Cyberpunk 2077 and now The Witcher 4, as well as our other projects. But because we knew The Witcher 4 would take time, we saw a gap in our release calendar where Songs of the Past could go. Thankfully, we were able to find the right partner to help execute it.” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s easier when nobody’s watching’: inside the secretive and sublime freak-folk of @
data.description: Their un-Googlable, very online name is the antithesis of this earthy duo’s sublime art-folk. Like their emotionally ambiguous music, the pair don’t give up their mysteries easily • The best music of autumn 2026: Johnny Marr, Phoebe Bridgers, Rachel Chinouriri and more • See all of our unmissable autumn arts recommendations here Victoria Rose arrives at Philadelphia’s 30th St Station and apologises for the sticky streaks covering her car’s interior. She’s a beekeeper, and it’s just propolis, a resinous sealant for gaps in the hive. Her bandmate, Stone Filipczak, is riding shotgun, and her protective gear occupies the rear passenger seat. We’re heading to one of their favourite spots, an Ethiopian restaurant that doubles as a venue. The dining room quickly gets boisterous – a challenge for our interview given that Filipczak and Rose are relatively soft speakers, and not wildly keen to divulge specifics about the music they make as @. Like Rose’s bees, they’re a secretive and self-sustaining pair. As you might guess, @ is pronounced “at”. It’s a tough Google. The name, Filipczak explains, came from “a vision of an @ sign on a kick drum head”. Not that they have any need for one: @’s art-folk is rooted in acoustic guitar, woodwinds and vocal harmonies that furrow and frolic. Their fantastic second album, Autosmile, is their first with the venerated indie label 4AD. (The name is a reference to a meme showing a dopey sunflower: “When you and gang faded and auto smile gets turn on …”) Continue reading...

data.title: Tim Dowling: my TV contract has run out – and so has my patience
data.description: I need to buy a smart television big enough to read ransom notes – and I’m taking no prisoners Fourteen years ago, I received a text from my eldest son claiming he’d just found the TV face down on the sitting room floor, destroyed. I didn’t entirely buy his theory about the dogs being responsible – I discovered a football lying suspiciously near the crime scene – but it was a problem I needed to solve before my wife returned from a business trip. That was the last time I bought a new television. It still works, but it’s small by today’s standards, to the extent that it’s impossible to read the contents of a ransom note held by a detective in a drama. As TVs have expanded, the ransom notes have got smaller; I often have to pause the programme, get up and put my nose to the screen. Continue reading...

There have been 474 confirmed cases and one death linked to the current outbreak, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), with the latest investigations suggesting it is associated with eating imported eggs in cafes and restaurants. data.title: Choking is sold to teens as a safe sexual practice. The research says it never is
data.description: More and more young people are engaging in sexual strangulation. But experts say there’s no safe pressure – and we have to start talking to teenagers about it When touching someone’s throat, it can only take the pressure of a handshake to cause serious injury, unconsciousness or death. These injuries, which include brain damage and stroke, are often internal and invisible, showing up days or even months after the initial incident occurred. Experts say many who participate in sexual choking are not aware of the risks. Choking or sexual strangulation is common among young people, says Prof Heather Douglas of the Melbourne Law School. In a 2024 survey of 4,702 Australians aged between 18 and 35, she and her research team found that 57% reported ever having experienced sexual strangulation; 51% reported ever having strangled a partner and 43.9% reported participating in both. Continue reading...

data.title: Adele Parks: ‘If I could ​edit my pas​t, I’d be fitter younger – I​ would have been hotter’
data.description: The author on the habit she can’t control, the writer she’s never read, and the true love of her life (it’s not her husband) Born in North Yorkshire, Adele Parks, 57, studied English at the University of Leicester then worked in advertising. In 2000, she published her debut novel, Playing Away, and has since written a book every year. Her latest is Eyes on You. Her work has been translated into 31 languages and in 2022 she was awarded the MBE for services to literature. She is an ambassador for charities promoting literacy including the National Literacy Trust, which is collaborating with the Department for Education on the National Year of Reading 2026. Parks is married with a son, and lives in Surrey. What is the trait you most deplore in yourself? Speaking negatively to myself. Continue reading...

data.title: Sweetener used in chewing gum and jam linked to strokes and heart attacks
data.description: High blood levels of xylitol associated with higher risk of major cardiovascular events, in largest study of its kind A common sweetener used in products such as chewing gum, toothpaste, jam, yoghurts and ice-cream has been linked to an increased risk of strokes, heart attacks and death. data.title: A wooden relic that survived the sack of Jerusalem's First Temple was unearthed by archaeologists, now they are finding shocking answers

By analyzing the growth rings, researchers have accurately dated this crucial archaeological evidence, providing an extraordinary link to Jerusalem's rich and ancient history.

data.title: Scientists spent 100 years discovering animals, reshaping where we see Earth’s biodiversity hotspots
data.description: A groundbreaking study has unveiled that taxonomic advancements have reshaped worldwide biodiversity maps over the last century. While reptile and amphibian diversity has markedly changed, bird and mammal distributions have remained mostly unchanged. Australia and Southeast Asia have been identified as key biodiversity hotspots for these groups. Moreover, factors influencing species richness are also shifting, with precipitation emerging as more crucial.

data.title: Estudo faz o retrato mais completo dos sacrifícios humanos no Império Inca
data.description: Por volta de 1450, três jovens indígenas foram sacrificados pelo Império Inca em duas montanhas do Chile . Uma nova pesquisa combinou uma série de análises químicas e anatômicas para reconstruir em detalhes os últimos meses de vida dessas crianças e adolescentes, e os resultados reforçam a ideia de que as mortes aconteceram no fim de uma longa peregrinação cerimonial, cujo objetivo era reforçar a aura de domínio imperial sobre vastas regiões sul-americanas. Leia mais (08/29/2026 - 06h00)

data.title: Uganda firar – fritt från ebolasmitta

data.title: Kan nya kungen rädda Norges skandaliserade kungahus?
data.description: Utanför slottet i Oslo vajar den norska flaggan på halvstång. Det är fredag den 28 augusti och den 89-årige kung Harald har just dött. Nu är det upp till sonen Haakon att ta över tronen. Men han gör det i ett läge där det norska kungahuset är historiskt impopulärt – efter en hektisk tid präglad av flera omskakande och allvarliga skandaler. Hur ska det gå för honom och hans fru Mette-Marit? Programledare: Elinor Ahlborn. Med Karin Eriksson, Nordenreporter på DN. Producent: Sabina Marmullakaj.

data.title: Fei-Fei Li: de ‘peetmoeder van AI’ die computers leerde kijken en nu bouwt aan de volgende fase
data.description: AI-pionier Fei-Fei Li maakte furore met ImageNet; ze leerde computers ‘kijken’. AI moet de mensheid dienen, vindt Li, die zich profileert als de nuchtere stem tussen techleiders die utopieën of juist nachtmerries verkopen. Maar ook zij is afhankelijk van financiers die rendement zoeken.

data.title: Rechter veegt vergeldingsactie Pentagon tegen AI-gigant Anthropic van tafel
data.description: Begin dit jaar liep een ruzie tussen Anthropic en het Amerikaanse ministerie van Defensie over de gebruiksvoorwaarden van AI-model Claude hoog op. De regering-Trump verklaarde Anthropic daarop tot „nationaal veiligheidsrisico” en zette het op een zwarte lijst. Dat was onwettig, oordeelde een federale rechter vrijdag.

data.title: Noční ruský útok u Buči zabil 27 lidí včetně starosty, jenž pomáhal po první vlně dronů
data.description: Při nočním ruském útoku na oblast kolem ukrajinského města Buča poblíž Kyjeva zahynulo nejméně 27 lidí. Dalších 42 lidí bylo zraněno. Z oblasti zasažené útokem se evakuuje více než 380 dospělých i dětí. Uvedl v sobotu šéf správy Kyjevské oblasti Tymur Tkačenko. Mezi obětmi je podle něj i starosta Dmytrivky Taras Didyč, který pomáhal s evakuací po první vlně útoku.

data.title: Pětice lezců uvázla v noci v Adršpašských skalách. Jeden zůstal viset na laně
data.description: Náročnou noční záchranu pětice lidí mají za sebou hasiči v Adršpachu. Tři ženy a dva muži strávili na skalním útvaru Milenci více než deset hodin. Jedna z osob při pokusu o slanění zůstala viset několik metrů nad zemí, další čtyři lidé čekali těsně pod vrcholem. Zásah skončil kolem čtvrt na šest ráno.

data.title: V noci nejvíc pršelo na jihu Moravy a na pomezí středních a východních Čech
data.description: V Česku od pátečního večera spadlo místy až 25 milimetrů srážek, ještě víc pršelo na jihu Moravy a na pomezí středních a východních Čech. Na síti X o tom v sobotu informoval Český hydrometeorologický ústav (ČHMÚ).

data.title: Aliance je schopná okamžitě bránit své území, říká český velvyslanec při NATO
data.description: Severoatlantická aliance (NATO) je schopná okamžitě a účinně bránit své území v případě například ruského vojenského útoku, řekl český velvyslanec při NATO David Konecký. Rozsáhlý konflikt mezi NATO a Ruskem v příštích letech nepředpokládá, podmínkou je podle něj ale další posilování aliančního odstrašení.

data.description: Německé vládní strany volají po posílení evropské ochrany před nekalou soutěží a po opatřeních na podporu výrobců automobilů. Podle parlamentních zdrojů jsou návrhy namířeny především proti čínským nadbytečným výrobním kapacitám, ale Čína v dokumentu přímo zmíněna není.

data.title: Soul plánuje v demilitarizované zóně mírový festival, u sousedů řeší spíše výrobu
data.description: Pohraniční oblast demilitarizované zóny (DMZ) mezi Jižní Koreou a KLDR zažije letos na podzim první ročník nového Festivalu míru (Peace Festa). Akci pořádá jihokorejské ministerstvo kultury, sportu a cestovního ruchu společně s místními provinciemi. Cílem organizátorů je, aby návštěvníci prožili region skrze přírodu, místní život a reflexi, spíše než skrze jeho historii rozdělení.

data.title: Česko zaplatilo za covidové vakcíny 19 miliard, využilo jich méně než polovinu
data.description: Česko zaplatilo za covidové vakcíny od roku 2020 zhruba 19 miliard korun. Na základě letos končící smlouvy ze začátku pandemie odebralo 41 milionů dávek, využilo jich méně než polovinu.

data.title: Trump oznámil dohodu s Venezuelou, USA získají obří množství ropy
data.description: Spojené státy uzavřely ropnou dohodu s Venezuelou. Zajistily si tak většinovou kontrolu nad více než 65 miliardami barelů z prokázaných venezuelských zásob ropy. To odpovídá zhruba pětině celkových prokázaných ropných rezerv této latinskoamerické země. Oznámil to v sobotu americký prezident Donald Trump na své sociální síti Truth Social. Uvedl rovněž, že jde o největší ropnou dohodu ve světové historii.

data.title: Globus odmaká školní přípravy za vás: Stačí poslat e-mail a do 24 hodin máte hotovo

data.title: Obce chystají past na kamiony. Ty, které porušují zákaz, mají chytat zvláštní kamery
data.description: Stovky obcí po celém Česku roky marně přihlížejí, jak jimi i přes zákazy denně projíždějí stovky kamionů objíždějící ucpané silnice nebo se vyhýbající placení mýta. Obce v prstenci okolo Brna, které mají stejný problém, teď připravují řešení: do ulic chtějí nainstalovat jako vůbec první v České republice speciální chytré kamery.

data.title: Plakaly tisíce lidí v ulicích, plakalo i nebe. Norové doprovodili rakev zesnulého krále
data.description: Ulice Osla v pátek večer navzdory silnému dešti zaplnily tisíce Norů, aby doprovodily rakev s tělem zesnulého oblíbeného krále Haralda V. na cestě z nemocnice do královského paláce. Harald, kterému bylo 89 let, v pátek ráno zemřel v Univerzitní nemocnici v Oslu.

data.title: Českem procházejí intenzivní bouřky, meteorologové varují před nárazy větru a kroupami
data.description: Českem procházejí intenzivní bouřky. Od Šumavy postupují rychle k severovýchodu. Meteorologové varovali především před silnými nárazy větru. Objevit se mohou i kroupy o velikosti přes dva centimetry, na jihozápadě Čech může vítr dosáhnout rychlosti až kolem 25 metrů za sekundu. Vyskytnout se může také přívalový déšť.

data.title: Rusové opět stojí fronty na benzin, Zelenskyj chce 1000 úderů denně
data.description: Ukrajina provedla od začátku srpna 21 úderů na ruské rafinerie, což je rekordní počet za jediný měsíc. Ukrajinské drony přitom zasáhly čtyři z deseti největších zpracovatelů, jejichž úkolem je zásobovat nejhustěji osídlené a průmyslově rozvinuté regiony Ruska. Ty se tak letos potýkají už s druhou vlnou nedostatku pohonných hmot během letní motoristické sezony.

data.title: Jako v roce 2022. Rusové prchají do Gruzie a Arménie, chtějí uniknout mobilizaci
data.description: Rusové začínají ve světle spekulací o nadcházející mobilizaci opouštět svoji zemi. Naznačují to zprávy z Gruzie či Arménie o růstu počtu obyvatel a zvyšujícím se zájmu Rusů o tamní nemovitosti. Makléři to přirovnávají k situaci, která nastala v roce 2022, kdy ruský prezident Vladimir Putin oznámil částečnou mobilizaci.

data.title: Zázrak uprostřed katastrofy. Zelený domek odolal povodni, rodina přežila na balkóně
data.description: Zázrak v zeleném domku. Tak přezdívají rodinu, která přežila nepálskou katastrofu na balkóně domečku, který dokola obklopila ničivá povodeň. data.title: Tragické povodně v Nepálu připravily o život 469 lidí. Téměř dva tisíce se pohřešují
data.description: V Nepálu je po ničivé povodni pohřešováno 1924 lidí. V aktualizované bilanci to v pátek uvedl tamní úřad pro zvládání katastrof s tím, že počet obětí vzrostl na 579. Přívalová povodeň ve středu zasáhla himálajské pohraničí Nepálu a čínského Tibetu, přičemž čínské úřady dříve oznámily pět obětí a 558 pohřešovaných.

data.title: Švýcarsko zasáhla ničivá bouře. Padaly obrovské kroupy, zranily na 40 lidí
data.description: Bouřka s rychlostí větru až 142 kilometrů v hodině v pátek vyvracela ve Švýcarsku stromy i betonové stožáry elektrického vedení. Až šesticentimetrové kroupy zranily na 40 lidí, jednu ženu vážně zranil padající strom, napsala agentura DPA. Krupobití bylo obzvláště silné v kantonu Curych, kde většinu z asi 40 zraněných tvoří děti.

data.title: Tohle jsme tu nezažili, situace je zoufalá, líčí z Nepálu humanitární pracovnice
data.description: Záplavy v Nepálu mají na svědomí stovky lidských životů, místní lidé se ukrývají v tunelech a na kopcích. Na místě jsou záchranáři a humanitární organizace, včetně Člověka v tísni. „Povodně, které zažíváme, jsme tu dosud nezažili. Rozsah poškození je pro nás devastující,“ popisuje z Nepálu v rozhovoru pro iDNES.cz zástupkyně organizace Sajana Shrestha.

data.title: Islanďané jsou rozpolcení nad obnovením jednání s EU, vyplývá z nového průzkumu
data.description: Těsná většina islandských voličů by nepodpořila obnovení jednání o členství země v Evropské unii, vyplynulo z nového průzkumu. data.title: Libya’s central bank chief resigns
data.description:
TRIPOLI: The governor of Libya’s central bank, Naji Issa, has resigned without giving a reason, several reports said on Monday.
	Private TV channel Al-Ahrar said Issa had confirmed his resignation.
	Issa and vice-governor Miree Al-Barasee were appointed by Libya’s parliament, which is based in the east of the divided country, in September 2024.
	His appointment was part of a deal backed by the United Nations that ended a standoff over Libya’s oil production and a deep financial crisis.

data.title: Trump insists Netanyahu relationship ‘very good’ despite Gaza rift
data.description:
WASHINGTON, United States: President Donald Trump insisted on Monday that his relationship with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is “very good” despite the Israeli leader’s rejection of a US-led Gaza plan.
	“The relationship is very good,” Trump said in response to a shouted question from a journalist at the end of an Oval Office event.
	After more than a week of gradually escalating criticism, Netanyahu explicitly stated on Sunday that he opposed the Gaza plan, which called for Israel to begin pulling back forces in tandem with disarmament by Hamas.

data.title: Final election phase begins in Pakistan-administered Kashmir despite banned group’s boycott call
data.description:

data.title: Can Al-Burhan’s Sudanese national dialogue turn military gains into a political settlement?
data.description:
LONDON: More than three years after Sudan descended into civil war, army chief Gen. Abdel Fattah Al-Burhan is pushing for a broad national dialogue aimed at rebuilding the country’s political institutions and laying the foundations for a civilian transition.

	Talks could begin as early as August, with preparatory consultations already involving political groups, technocrats, Sufi leaders, traditional authorities, academics, professionals, civil society representatives and independent figures.

data.title: Crise anglophone : un tribunal fédéral américain condamne trois Américains d’origine camerounaise
data.description: © DR Jugés coupables d'avoir fourni du soutien financier et logistique pour la fabrication et l'utilisation des engins explosifs improvisés au Cameroun, ils n'échappent pas à de lourdes peines. Ils écopent des peines allant de cinq à 15 ans de prison ferme. Francis Chenyi âgé de 52 ans, Lah Nestor Langmi, 49 ans tombent sous le coup d'une condamnation de 15 ans de prison chacun. Tandis que Claude Ngenevu Chi, 43 ans, doit purger 63 mois de prison correspondant à un peu plus de 5 ans. Après avoir purgé les différentes peines, les trois condamnés seront soumis chacun à trois ans de liberté surveillée. Ainsi a décidé le tribunal fédéral de Kansas City dans le Missouri. Il est reproché aux trois ressortissants camerounais d'avoir appartenu à un réseau de financement et de fourniture de la logistique au profit des combattants séparatistes qui opèrent dans les régions du Nord-Ouest et du Sud-Ouest. Ils ont exercé des missions de coordination des opérations de fabrication des engins explosifs improvisés ainsi que de la formation des personnes en vue de leur utilisation, apprend-on de sources médiatiques. Des mêmes sources, cette coordination s'étend aussi à des attaques à l'aide de ces explosifs en ciblant plusieurs villes du Nord-Ouest et à proximité du stade devant accueillir la CAN 2021 dans la région du Sud-Ouest. Aussi, la justice reproche à ces trois hommes d'avoir coordonné des opérations de transfert des fonds des États-Unis vers le Cameroun. Des fonds qui ont servi à réaliser des projets d'attaques évoqués plus haut. De manière individuelle, la justice reproche à Langmi d'avoir participé à la coordination des opérations d'enlèvements dont celui du chef traditionnel Fonmbam Aforteka et celui du cardinal Christian Tumi de regrettée mémoire. Pour la commission de ces faits, Chenyi aurait fourni une contribution financière. Ce sont ainsi trois financiers de plus de la crise anglophone qui sont condamnés par la justice américaine dans le cadre du règlement de la crise. Depuis quelques années, d'autres Camerounais ont écopé des condamnations à des peines diverses presque pour les mêmes motifs. Che Ernest Banhary et Edith Ngang ont écopé de quatre ans de prison ferme. En 2024, une trentaine de leaders séparatistes ont été traduits devant les juridictions américaines à la suite de plusieurs plaintes déposées par le cabinet Me Nsahlai à la demande de l'Etat camerounais. Les États-Unis se sont engagés à poursuivre juger et condamner ces hommes suspectés d'avoir participé à financer ou à commettre des actes terroristes sur le territoire camerounais. Cet article Crise anglophone : un tribunal fédéral américain condamne trois Américains d’origine camerounaise est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Coopération Cameroun-UNFPA : le 9e Programme Pays validé à 50 millions USD
data.description: © DR 50 millions de dollars, 3 piliers stratégiques, un partenariat depuis 1969. Le Conseil d'Administration de l'UNFPA a approuvé le 27 août 2026 à New York le 9e Programme de Coopération avec le Cameroun (2027-2031), aligné sur la SND30 et l'UNSDCF. C’est le quitus officiel. Le Conseil d’Administration de l’UNFPA a validé le 27 août 2026 le nouveau Programme de Coopération Pays (CPD9) axé sur le bien-être des populations et le dividende démographique. Fruit d’une concertation menée par le MINEPAT et le MINREX en alignement avec le cadre UNSDCF 2027-2031 et la Stratégie Nationale de Développement SND30, le programme pérennise un partenariat historique initié en 1969. Présentant l’aval du gouvernement à New York, la Mission Permanente du Cameroun a déclaré : "Ma délégation note avec satisfaction l'alignement du document sur la SND30 et le cadre UNSDCF. Le Gouvernement exprime son ferme soutien au 9e Programme Pays et invite le Conseil à l'approuver." Doté d’un budget indicatif de 50 millions USD, le CPD9 vise trois piliers d’ici 2031 : qualité des soins et santé reproductive avec accès universel à la planification familiale et réduction des décès maternels, égalité de genre et autonomisation avec éradication des violences basées sur le genre, et données démographiques pour des politiques publiques informées. Pour accompagner l’expansion, Yaoundé offre un nouveau siège moderne à l’UNFPA, s’affirmant comme partenaire clé grâce à la mobilisation conjointe du MINEPAT, MINREX, MINSANTE, MINPROFF, MINJEC et MINFI. Cet article Coopération Cameroun-UNFPA : le 9e Programme Pays validé à 50 millions USD est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: La tripartite RDC-HCR-Tanzanie insiste sur le retour volontaire des réfugiés congolais
data.description: Au total, 87 650 réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile congolais vivent dans le camp de Nyarugusu dans la région de Kigoma en Tanzanie. Ceux qui le souhaitent seront rapatriés progressivement en RDC suivant un plan qui sera mis en œuvre en fonction des disponibilités des ressources. data.title: Guerra con Irán provoca grave crisis financiera en el ejército de Estados Unidos

data.title: Unión Eléctrica prevé una afectación de 2350 MW para este viernes
data.description: En el día de ayer se afectó el servicio por déficit de capacidad durante las 24 horas. Para este viernes la Unión Eléctrica en el horario de máxima demanda prevé una disponibilidad de 930 MW con una demanda máxima de 3250 MW, para un déficit de 2320 MW, por lo que de mantenerse las condiciones previstas se pronostica una afectación de 2350 MW en este horario. The post Unión Eléctrica prevé una afectación de 2350 MW para este viernes first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: Abogado señalado de revelar identidad de testigo protegido se defenderá en libertad en SPS
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Honduras. El profesional del derecho Osman Josué Laínez Herrera se defenderá en libertad luego de que un juez le impusiera medidas cautelares sustitutivas a la detención judicial por su presunta participación en la revelación de la identidad de un testigo protegido. La resolución se conoció este viernes 28 de agosto, durante la Audiencia de Declaración de Imputado celebrada en el Juzgado de Letras Penal con Competencia Nacional en Materia de Criminalidad Organizada, Medio Ambiente y Corrupción, en San Pedro Sula. Laínez Herrera fue sometido a un proceso judicial por el delito de revelación de identidad de testigo protegido, en perjuicio de la administración de justicia del Estado de Honduras. Tras escuchar los planteamientos de las partes, el juez determinó imponer al profesional del derecho una medida cautelar distinta a la detención judicial, por lo que no deberá permanecer privado de libertad mientras continúa el proceso. Como parte de las medidas impuestas, el abogado deberá cumplir con la presentación periódica cada 15 días ante la autoridad correspondiente. Asimismo, el juzgado ordenó su inmediata libertad, al considerar procedente la aplicación de medidas sustitutivas durante el desarrollo de la causa. Durante la audiencia, el Ministerio Público había solicitado la imposición de una medida cautelar limitativa de la libertad para el imputado, mientras que la defensa técnica se opuso a la petición fiscal. La defensa presentó elementos relacionados con el arraigo de su representado y solicitó que se mantuviera su estado de inocencia mientras avanza el proceso judicial. El caso también tuvo un cambio de competencia, debido a que el juez de Letras Penal con Jurisdicción Nacional determinó declinar el conocimiento de la causa y remitir el expediente al Juzgado de Letras de lo Penal. La decisión implica que el proceso continuará ante la jurisdicción correspondiente, donde deberán desarrollarse las siguientes etapas establecidas por la legislación hondureña. La Audiencia Inicial fue programada para las 9:00 de la mañana del 17 de septiembre de 2026, fecha en la que las partes deberán comparecer nuevamente ante el órgano jurisdiccional.

data.title: Esta es la razón por la que el interconector El Carmen está paralizado en San Pedro Sula
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Honduras. De nuevo, los conductores que transitan por el corredor Los Cármenes-Segundo Anillo vivieron una mañana infernal provocada por el congestionamiento que dejó la protesta de de un grupo de pobladores. Un día después de que el alcalde Roberto Contreras habilitara un paso provisional y anunciara que se terminarían los congestionamientos, el caos volvió y muchas personas llegaron tarde a sus trabajos otros optaron por regresar a sus casas. Sumado a ello la misma municipalidad había anunciado un cierre temporal en ese sector por la construcción de la rotonda, específicamente en el acceso del bordo hacia la Santa Marta. Pero esta vez la protesta se debe a que los pobladores solicitan a Siglo 21 más obras para el sector y la próxima finalización de los trabajos inconclusos. Por lo menos, esa fue la explicación de la oficina de Relaciones Públicas de la alcaldía. “Nosotros estamos cansados ​​de este tráfico y que se tiren la pelota ni siquiera porque muchos funcionarios viven en estas colonias se ponen las pilas y acá culpan a uno ya otro lo que queremos es que ayuden y terminen”, dice Carlos García , un conductor que permaneció más de dos horas en el tráfico. Es real que el consorcio Siglo 21 construye un interconector exactamente en el puente del río Bermejo y que la obra se ha paralizado porque la municipalidad y la Secretaría de Infraestructura y Transporte (SIT) deben liberar el derecho de vía para poder continuar con los trabajos y no lo han hecho. La obra vial comenzó en 2025 con el objetivo de aliviar el congestionamiento vehicular en la zona de Los Cármenes. El proyecto comprende un retorno subterráneo tipo túnel y un canal de alivio. La obra tiene retraso por la lentitud en despejar el derecho de vía pues no han desalojado a las familias quienes esperan una reubicación digna. Según los mismos pobladores del bordo anexos a la Bográn,son mas o menos 130 personas que residen en el lugar  También señaló que, pese a ese registro, no han recibido información directa sobre el lugar donde serían trasladados y han preguntado varias veces. Por su parte, el consorcio Siglo 21 emitió un comunicado en el que se solidarizó con los vecinos y reiteró el compromiso de terminar el interconector. El comunicado señala que la preocupación expresada por los vecinos es legítima debido a la pausa en las obras del interconector El Carmen, porque es un proyecto vital para aliviar el tráfico, mejorar la seguridad vial y elevar la calidad de vida de miles de familias en ese sector. Siglo 21 aclara de forma categórica que la no continuidad de los trabajos no se debe a la falta de voluntad ni de recursos por parte del consorcio. “La obra civil se encuentra paralizada debido a que aún no se ha completado la liberación del derecho de vía requerida en la zona del proyecto”, dice el comunicado, Además, pide respetuosamente a las autoridades competentes ya las partes involucradas agilizar la liberación definitiva de los terrenos correspondientes al derecho de vía. Los pobladores piden a las autoridades que se pongan de acuerdo, concluyan la obra e informen correctamente cuál es la situación. Está claro que se tienen que realizar desalojos en la zona de viviendas que están en el derecho de vía, explicaron. Mientras se construye la rotonda, según el alcalde Roberto Contreras, los conductores deben usar una vía alterna recién habilitada. Quienes vienen de Los Cármenes deben girar a la derecha unos 100 metros antes de la rotonda; es una ruta habilitada únicamente de salida. Contreras dijo que, con esa solución temporal, el congestionamiento en la zona se terminaba. "Aquí estamos desde temprano resolviendo un problema real. Esta rotonda ordenará el tráfico, porque la gente estaba tardando hasta una hora y media en llegar a sus trabajos", dijo Contreras. data.translatedTitle: Esta es la razón por la que el interconector El Carmen está paralizado en San Pedro Sula
data.translatedDescription: San Pedro Sula, Honduras. De nuevo, los conductores que transitan por el corredor Los Cármenes-Segundo Anillo vivieron una mañana infernal provocada por el congestionamiento que dejó la protesta de de un grupo de pobladores. Un día después de que el alcalde Roberto Contreras habilitara un paso provisional y anunciara que se terminarían los congestionamientos, el caos volvió y muchas personas llegaron tarde a sus trabajos otros optaron por regresar a sus casas. Sumado a ello la misma municipalidad había anunciado un cierre temporal en ese sector por la construcción de la rotonda, específicamente en el acceso del bordo hacia la Santa Marta. Pero esta vez la protesta se debe a que los pobladores solicitan a Siglo 21 más obras para el sector y la próxima finalización de los trabajos inconclusos. Por lo menos, esa fue la explicación de la oficina de Relaciones Públicas de la alcaldía. “Nosotros estamos cansados ​​de este tráfico y que se tiren la pelota ni siquiera porque muchos funcionarios viven en estas colonias se ponen las pilas y acá culpan a uno ya otro lo que queremos es que ayuden y terminen”, dice Carlos García , un conductor que permaneció más de dos horas en el tráfico. Es real que el consorcio Siglo 21 construye un interconector exactamente en el puente del río Bermejo y que la obra se ha paralizado porque la municipalidad y la Secretaría de Infraestructura y Transporte (SIT) deben liberar el derecho de vía para poder continuar con los trabajos y no lo han hecho. La obra vial comenzó en 2025 con el objetivo de aliviar el congestionamiento vehicular en la zona de Los Cármenes. El proyecto comprende un retorno subterráneo tipo túnel y un canal de alivio. La obra tiene retraso por la lentitud en despejar el derecho de vía pues no han desalojado a las familias quienes esperan una reubicación digna. Según los mismos pobladores del bordo anexos a la Bográn,son mas o menos 130 personas que residen en el lugar  También señaló que, pese a ese registro, no han recibido información directa sobre el lugar donde serían trasladados y han preguntado varias veces. Por su parte, el consorcio Siglo 21 emitió un comunicado en el que se solidarizó con los vecinos y reiteró el compromiso de terminar el interconector. El comunicado señala que la preocupación expresada por los vecinos es legítima debido a la pausa en las obras del interconector El Carmen, porque es un proyecto vital para aliviar el tráfico, mejorar la seguridad vial y elevar la calidad de vida de miles de familias en ese sector. Siglo 21 aclara de forma categórica que la no continuidad de los trabajos no se debe a la falta de voluntad ni de recursos por parte del consorcio. “La obra civil se encuentra paralizada debido a que aún no se ha completado la liberación del derecho de vía requerida en la zona del proyecto”, dice el comunicado, Además, pide respetuosamente a las autoridades competentes ya las partes involucradas agilizar la liberación definitiva de los terrenos correspondientes al derecho de vía. Los pobladores piden a las autoridades que se pongan de acuerdo, concluyan la obra e informen correctamente cuál es la situación. Está claro que se tienen que realizar desalojos en la zona de viviendas que están en el derecho de vía, explicaron. Mientras se construye la rotonda, según el alcalde Roberto Contreras, los conductores deben usar una vía alterna recién habilitada. Quienes vienen de Los Cármenes deben girar a la derecha unos 100 metros antes de la rotonda; es una ruta habilitada únicamente de salida. Contreras dijo que, con esa solución temporal, el congestionamiento en la zona se terminaba. "Aquí estamos desde temprano resolviendo un problema real. Esta rotonda ordenará el tráfico, porque la gente estaba tardando hasta una hora y media en llegar a sus trabajos", dijo Contreras. El jefe edilicio explicó que la habilitación de esta vía fue posible gracias al acuerdo alcanzado con propietarios de terrenos cercanos, quienes permitieron el uso del espacio para facilitar el tránsito mientras se termina la rotonda.

data.title: El dólar supera los L27 y genera preocupación en Honduras
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Honduras. Tal como lo habían advertido el Banco Central de Honduras (BCH) y economistas, el precio del dólar en venta alcanzó los 27.0010 lempiras este viernes 28 de agosto de 2026. Ante este nuevo nivel del tipo de cambio, expertos anticipan efectos inmediatos en la economía hondureña. La mañana de este viernes, los hondureños se encontraron con que el precio del dólar de venta cruzó la barrera de los 27 lempiras. El precio oficial fijado por el Banco Central de Honduras (BCH) es de L27.0010 para la venta y L26.8667 para la compra . Analistas habían sido conservadores y esperaban que este deslizamiento de la moneda ocurriera a finales de septiembre o incluso a inicios de octubre; sin embargo, el movimiento se produjo antes de lo previsto. Roberto Lagos, presidente del BCH, declaró recientemente que el tipo de cambio seguirá deslizándose y no se mantendrá fijo, debido a que existe un deslizamiento natural de la economía. “Si yo tuviera el tipo de cambio fijo, perdería reservas y si pierdo reservas como le hago frente a las importaciones de combustibles, a los compromisos de país y endeudamiento”. Al 20 de agosto de 2026, las reservas internacionales netas del BCH alcanzaron los 11,669.9 millones de dólares, un aumento de 1,364.1 millones respecto al 27 de enero, con una cobertura equivalente a 6.7 meses de importaciones. Según el Pulso Económico del BCH, al 20 de agosto el tipo de cambio de referencia fue de L26.8368 por dólar, frente a L26.3737 al cierre de 2025. Esto representa una depreciación acumulada de 1.76%. En términos interanuales, la depreciación fue de 3.46%, menor al 4.77% registrado un año antes. El precio del dólar depende, principalmente, de cuántas divisas ingresan al país y cuántas se necesitan para realizar pagos en el exterior. Las remesas, las exportaciones, la inversión extranjera y el turismo generan dólares, mientras que las importaciones, la compra de combustibles, los bienes de capital y el pago de deuda externa generan demanda de divisas. Un dólar más caro significa que los importadores necesitan más lempiras para comprar productos en el exterior. Esto puede elevar los costos de combustibles, materias primas, maquinaria y productos terminados, y parte de ese aumento puede trasladarse a los consumidores. Si los precios suben más rápido que los salarios, los hogares pierden poder adquisitivo porque pueden comprar menos con la misma cantidad de dinero. Para quienes reciben remesas, un dólar más caro significa más lempiras por cada dólar recibido, aunque ese beneficio puede reducirse si también aumentan los precios. Dante Mossi, expresidente del BCIE, escribió en su cuenta de X: “Bueno contra todo pronóstico justo antes del mes de la patria el precio de venta del dólar sobrepaso la barrera de L27, hoy L27,0010/US$. Y que hará el Banco Central de Honduras, dejar que la tendencia siga acelerándose”, cuestionó Mossi. Amparo Canales, expresidenta del Colegio Hondureño de Economistas, declaró que, de mantenerse la actual tendencia, el lempira podría cerrar el año con un tipo de cambio superior a los 27.15 o 27.30 lempiras por dólar, lo que tendría repercusiones en el precio de los productos importados. Expertos señalan que el efecto es inmediato porque Honduras depende de las importaciones de productos y servicios, por lo que el incremento del tipo de cambio se traduce en un encarecimiento de los costos para la población. El sector mipyme, por su parte, vaticina el fracaso de más pequeños negocios debido a los altos costos de la energía eléctrica y advierte que el aumento del dólar encarece toda la cadena de producción.

data.title: Ingreso de humedad provocará lluvias la tarde de este viernes en varias regiones de Honduras
data.description: Tegucigalpa. El ambiente cálido y seco predominará este viernes 28 de agosto en la mayor parte del territorio hondureño, de acuerdo con el pronóstico oficial emitido por la Secretaría de Estado en los Despachos de Gestión de Riesgos y Contingencias Nacionales ( Copeco ). Según el reporte oficial del ente de previsión, “prevalecerán las condiciones secas y cálidas en la mayor parte del territorio nacional”, por lo que se esperan altas temperaturas durante la mayor parte de la jornada en diversas regiones del país. No obstante, las autoridades meteorológicas advierten un leve cambio en el clima en horas de la tarde debido al ingreso de una humedad. “Por la tarde, el ingreso de humedad proveniente del mar Caribe provocará precipitaciones débiles sobre áreas de las regiones del noroccidente, norte y oriente”, detalló la institución en su informe diario. En cuanto a las condiciones marítimas, la Copeco informó que el oleaje en las costas del país mantendrá parámetros normales y estables. Tanto en el litoral caribeño como en el golfo de Fonseca se registrarán olas con alturas que oscilarán entre 1 y 3 pies, garantizando actividad segura para la navegación de calado menor. Asimismo, el informe astronómico indica que los hondureños contaron con el inicio de la salida del sol desde las 05:37 a.m. y el ocultamiento está previsto para las 06:03 p.m. Además, la fase lunar actual se mantiene en luna llena durante este cierre de semana. Las autoridades recomiendan a la población mantenerse hidratada ante las elevadas temperaturas de la mañana y cargar paraguas por las lluvias de la tarde . Asimismo, piden a la población de los sectores donde se registrarán precipitaciones tomar las medidas necesarias para proteger sus vidas en caso de cualquier eventualidad que pueda ponerlos en riesgo.

data.title: ¿Cuándo entrará en vigencia el descuento en la matrícula para adultos mayores?
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Honduras. El Congreso Nacional de Honduras aprobó a finales de julio un descuento del 50% en la matrícula vehicular anual para los adultos mayores, jubilados y pensionados. La medida es esperada por muchos hondureños que buscan acceder a este beneficio durante el período de matrícula 2026 , que comenzó en julio con los vehículos cuyas placas terminan en 0 y 1. Sin embargo, aunque la medida fue aprobada a finales de julio, el decreto todavía no ha sido publicado en el diario oficial La Gaceta, por lo que aún no está vigente. Esto significa que los propietarios de vehículos que cumplen con las condiciones para recibir el beneficio todavía no pueden aplicarlo a su matrícula. El beneficio contempla una reducción del 50% en el pago de la matrícula vehicular para los adultos mayores, jubilados y pensionados. De acuerdo con lo establecido en la medida aprobada, se considera adulto mayor o de la tercera edad a la persona a partir de los 60 años, lo que incluye a quienes tienen entre 60 y 79 años, mientras que la cuarta edad corresponde a las personas a partir de los 80 años. El diputado Carlos Ledezma, secretario del Congreso Nacional, declaró a medios de comunicación que el proyecto fue aprobado, pero todavía no ha sido ratificado en acta debido a que deben modificarse ciertos artículos que están mal redactados. Además, señaló que la Secretaría de Desarrollo Social (Sedesol) revisará los artículos antes de su publicación. “Esperamos lo más pronto posible que sea revisado y enviado a La Gaceta”, dijo Ledezma el 19 de agosto. Sin embargo, hasta ahora el decreto continúa a la espera de su publicación. Ledezma también aseguró que, después de su aprobación, el decreto estaba siendo revisado por la Secretaría de Finanzas y el Instituto de la Propiedad (IP). Mientras tanto, los hondureños que esperan acceder al beneficio deberán continuar pagando la matrícula bajo las condiciones vigentes hasta que el decreto sea publicado. Los propietarios a quienes correspondió realizar el trámite en julio, con las terminaciones de placas 0 y 1, y en agosto, con las terminaciones 2 y 3, no han podido gozar del descuento. A Lourdes Hernández, de 62 años, le correspondía pagar este mes la matrícula vehicular, debido a que la terminación de su placa es 3. Ella esperaba que el decreto entrara en vigencia para poder gozar del descuento del 50%, ya que debía pagar cerca de L4,000. Sin embargo, al ver que agosto estaba por terminar, prefirió realizar el pago para evitar caer en mora y tener que pagar multas. “Me saldrá peor, porque si no pago este mes me van a cobrar multa. Ya no pude ver el beneficio, si es verdad que lo van a poner”, expresó Hernández. La expectativa está ahora en conocer si los propietarios de vehículos mayores de 60 años podrán acceder al beneficio a partir de septiembre, cuando corresponde el turno a las terminaciones de placas 4 y 5. Carlos Umaña, diputado del Partido Liberal, manifestó que la tardanza en la publicación también lo ha afectado, ya que le correspondió pagar la matrícula sin el descuento. Para recibir el beneficio, el vehículo debe estar registrado a nombre de la persona adulta mayor, jubilada o pensionada. Además, el propietario deberá presentar su carné o Documento Nacional de Identificación (DNI) ante las oficinas del Instituto de la Propiedad (IP), una vez que el decreto entre en vigencia. Desde las oficinas del IP informaron que, cuando el decreto sea publicado en La Gaceta, realizarán los ajustes necesarios en el sistema y lo anunciarán de manera oficial para informar a la población. Durante el primer mes de matrícula, correspondiente a julio y a los vehículos cuyas placas terminan en 0 y 1, cayeron en mora 63,060 usuarios , correspondientes a 76,226 placas, lo que representó una recaudación de L249.3 millones, de acuerdo con datos proporcionados por el IP a LA PRENSA. Sin embargo, 302,178 propietarios de vehículos cumplieron con la obligación, con una recaudación de L821.7 millones. Para agosto, las autoridades esperan el pago de 243,940 propietarios de vehículos y una recaudación de L709.7 millones. Es importante recordar que la amnistía vehicular, que duró dos meses y permitía a los propietarios liberarse del pago de multas, recargos e intereses por mora correspondientes a la matrícula de 2025 y años anteriores, venció el 25 de agosto.
